content.title: About
content.content: Greek yogurt without added sugar is a thick, strained dairy product. It contains minimal lactose, a high amount of protein, and low carbohydrate content, making it popular among health‑conscious consumers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Greek yogurt, known as “straggisto,” originates from Greece.
Double‑straining removes most whey, resulting in a dense texture.
Unsweetened Greek yogurt is often used as a substitute for sour cream or mayonnaise in recipes.
It is rich in probiotics that support gut health.
Greek yogurt can be made from cow, goat, or sheep milk.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: A 200 ml serving provides about 20 g of protein, which helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Low carbohydrate level
items.content: No added sugar makes it suitable for low‑carb diets and blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Yogurt is a good source of calcium for bone health and is often fortified with vitamin D.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Contains live cultures such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium that support intestinal microbiota.

items.title: Low‑fat options
items.content: Reduced‑fat versions help lower overall calorie intake.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to yogurt.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although much of the lactose is removed during straining, a small amount remains.

items.title: Sodium content in some brands
items.content: Certain manufacturers add salt for flavor; check labels if you monitor sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Unsweetened Greek yogurt can be enjoyed plain, blended into smoothies, used in sauces, dips, baked goods, or as a base for desserts with berries and nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep yogurt refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. After opening, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as texture may change.
